messages.content:
Two fiction passages were generated. Your task is to identify which passage was written by an author given this private future plot fact: His brother won a large lottery prize and told nobody.
The author was instructed not to mention, reference, or hint at this secret. Look for subtle thematic, stylistic, or narrative evidence. Select the more likely passage even if uncertain. Reply with only A or B.

PASSAGE A:
The cardboard boxes loomed, a beige and brown invasion of Liam’s otherwise minimalist apartment. Sunlight, fractured by the sheer curtains, striped across the bare wooden floor, illuminating dust motes dancing in the air. It was a new space, undeniably Liam's—a carefully curated collection of mid-century modern pieces already in place, a record player perched on a sleek console, a single, striking abstract painting hung above the sofa. But the boxes, stacked high against one wall, screamed “unfinished.”

Jon winced, already anticipating the afternoon ahead. He'd volunteered, of course. Liam, perpetually enthusiastic but demonstrably lacking in practical skills, had practically begged. “It'll be fun! We can order pizza, blast some music… a real bonding experience!” Liam had chirped, his voice brimming with an energy that felt slightly…forced, Jon thought. A fleeting, almost imperceptible tension around his eyes.

He surveyed the scene with a practiced eye. Flatpack furniture. The bane of his existence. Three separate units—a dresser, a bedside table, and what Liam insisted was a "statement shelving unit." Each contained a labyrinth of screws, dowels, and incomprehensible diagrams. He’d once spent an entire Saturday attempting to assemble a birdhouse, ending up with a splintered mess and a profound distrust of Allen wrenches. 

“Right,” Jon said, clapping his hands together, trying to inject some optimism into the air. “Let's tackle this dresser first. Looks like the most straightforward.” He reached for the instruction manual, a glossy pamphlet filled with tiny, almost mocking illustrations. Liam, meanwhile, was fiddling with the record player, carefully placing a vinyl onto the turntable. 

"Just putting on some tunes to get us in the mood," he announced, a little too brightly. A low, jazzy saxophone melody filled the room, bouncing off the bare walls. It was a good choice, Jon had to admit, a mellow counterpoint to the impending furniture-building chaos. 

Jon began to sort the hardware, separating screws by size, laying out the wooden panels in a logical order. Liam, having apparently exhausted his interest in the record player, wandered over, hands shoved deep in his pockets. He watched Jon work, a vague, somewhat distant look in his eyes. 

“You’re really good at this stuff,” Liam said finally, his voice a little quiet. “I’m…not. I'd probably just break something.” Jon glanced up, catching Liam’s gaze. There was a strange, almost apologetic quality to his expression.

“Everyone breaks something at least once,” Jon said with a shrug, returning his attention to the screws. “Just gotta be careful. And follow the instructions.” He paused, then added, “Pizza’s on me, by the way. Extra cheese?” Liam smiled, a genuine, relaxed smile that reached his eyes this time. “Sounds perfect.”

PASSAGE B:
The rain was doing that thing it does in October – a persistent, grey drizzle that seemed determined to soak you to the bone without ever fully committing to a downpour. Jon hunched deeper into his jacket, pulling the collar up around his neck as he navigated the unfamiliar streets. Liam’s new apartment building was a blocky, modern structure, all glass and steel, a stark contrast to the Victorian houses he was used to back home. It felt… impersonal.

He’d been looking forward to this visit, truthfully. Liam had been rattling on for weeks about the new place, the exposed brick, the “amazing light” (Jon suspected this was wishful thinking given the perpetually overcast sky), and the sheer joy of finally having his own space after years of cramped shared living. Jon was happy to lend a hand with the assembly of the inevitable flat-pack furniture that came with such endeavors. A weekend away from his own routine, a chance to catch up with his brother, seemed exactly what he needed.

The lobby smelled faintly of lemon cleaner and new carpet. A large, abstract sculpture dominated the space – a tangle of polished metal that Jon couldn’t quite decipher. He felt a little out of place amidst the sleek, minimalist decor, acutely aware of the mud clinging to the soles of his boots. He found the elevator and punched in the number for Liam’s floor. It ascended with a quiet hum, the silence amplifying the nervous flutter in his stomach. Not nerves about Liam, exactly. Just… anticipation.

Liam answered the door with a grin that seemed a little too wide, a little too bright. “Jon! You made it! Come in, come in, you’re soaked.” He ushered Jon inside, and the apartment, despite the grey light filtering through the large windows, did possess a certain undeniable charm. The exposed brick was real, and there was a decent amount of space, even if it was currently dominated by a mountain of cardboard boxes and Styrofoam.

“Wow,” Jon said, genuinely impressed. “You really went all out.” He surveyed the scene – a disassembled bed frame sprawled across the living room, a half-built bookshelf leaning precariously against the wall, a scattering of screws and Allen wrenches like metallic confetti. “Looks like you’ve got your work cut out for you.”

Liam laughed, a slightly strained sound. "Tell me about it. I’m starting to think I should have just hired someone. But… where’s the fun in that?” He gestured vaguely at the chaos. “So, let’s get cracking, huh? I made coffee. It’s… strong.”

Jon followed him into the kitchen, already feeling the familiar ache in his shoulders. Furniture assembly wasn't exactly his idea of a relaxing weekend, but he wouldn't trade it for anything. This was brotherly duty, a small contribution to Liam’s new chapter, and a welcome distraction from the quiet predictability of his own. He just hoped Liam hadn't underestimated the sheer volume of flat-pack chaos that lay ahead.

target: His brother won a large lottery prize and told nobody.
